name: Internal In-House Tooling
trigger_phrases: Our engineering team already built this
We have developer headcount to maintain this
root_cause: Engineering pride, NIH (Not Invented Here) syndrome, or misjudged maintenance costs.
reframe_strategy: Acknowledge engineering competence, then pivot to hidden ongoing maintenance toil and lost opportunity cost on customer-facing revenue features.
talk_track: That proves how critical this problem is to your leadership that you committed senior engineering headcount. Typically, engineering leaders tell us that maintaining custom internal tooling consumes 15-20% of senior developer bandwidth on bug fixes and maintenance rather than shipping customer-facing revenue features. If we could offload that maintenance burden while giving your engineers full API extensibility, would it be worth evaluating what that 20% capacity reallocation looks like on your Q4 product roadmap?

name: Competitor Discounting
trigger_phrases: Your price per seat is too high
We received a heavy discount from another vendor
root_cause: Commoditized feature comparison, lack of Cost of Inaction clarity.
reframe_strategy: Never compete in a bottom-feeding price war. Re-anchor license price against 3-year Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), migration costs, and downtime risk.
talk_track: If price per license were the only factor, that competitor would be the only vendor in the market. When enterprise clients choose our architecture, they aren't paying for software licenses; they are insuring against the $250k/hour downtime risk and hidden migration maintenance costs. Let's compare the 3-year Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) including migration engineering hours.

name: Total CFO Budget Freeze
trigger_phrases: All new spending is frozen until next fiscal year
Our CFO locked all department budgets
reframe_strategy: CFOs freeze expense lines, but aggressively approve self-amortizing projects that reduce existing operational waste or protect cash flows within the current period.
talk_track: Understood. Typically, budget freezes apply to new speculative projects, but CFOs always approve initiatives that directly reduce operational waste or protect existing cash flows. If we launched a lightweight 30-day proof-of-value that pays for itself through immediate cloud egress savings before the fiscal year ends, would your leadership consider reviewing that self-funding business case?
